record.original_question: Determine the geometrical thickness of the complete graph K_n, where each planar layer is drawn with straight-line edges and the same point set for the vertices.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2 Find the geometrical thickness of the complete graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A geometric drawing of a graph $G$ in the plane consists of placing the vertices as distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and drawing each edge as the straight-line segment between its endpoints. A geometric $k$-layer drawing of $G$ is a geometric drawing together with a partition of the edge set into $k$ classes (layers) such that, on the same fixed vertex point set, the edges in each individual layer form a planar straight-line drawing (i.e., no two edges of the same layer cross). The geometric thickness $\bar{\theta}(G)$ is the minimum $k$ for which such a drawing exists.

Determine $\bar{\theta}(K_n)$ as a function of $n$; that is, find a closed-form expression (or otherwise exactly characterize) the geometric thickness of the complete graph on $n$ vertices.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact geometric thickness of $K_n$ remains open. Known bounds give $\lceil n/5.646 + 0.342\rceil \le \bar{\theta}(K_n) \le \lceil n/4\rceil$, and exact values have been established only for small $n$ (n ≤ 12 and n ∈ {15,16}). No closed-form formula for general $n$ is known.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Thickness of Complete Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds ⌈n/5.646⌉ ≤ geometric thickness of K_n ≤ ⌈n/4⌉, with exact values for small n.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds are known but exact value of geometric thickness of K_n is not determined in general.

status_evidence.title: Thickness (graph theory) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Geometric thickness of complete graphs is known only within bounds, exact values for limited small cases.
status_evidence.claim: Exact determination of geometric thickness of K_n is an open problem.
